description: Get one saved survey respondent by `id` (from listSurveyTestConfigs or a survey result's configId), in full: the fields listSurveyTestConfigs returns plus `mission` (who the respondent is and how they feel) and `acceptance` (what counts as a pass). Use when: you want to explain what a survey test checks. Name its persona with getProfile. Read-only. Needs testing:read. Returns 404 if the config is not in your workspace.
name: getSurveyTestConfig

outputSchema.description:
A saved survey respondent: who this person is, how they feel, and how
they behave once a survey reaches them.

Survey testing REVERSES the direction of every other test in this API.
The customer's platform originates the survey and nopaque answers as
the member of the public being surveyed, so a survey config carries no
number to dial. Which of your vended numbers a run answers on, and
which of the customer's numbers originates, are chosen when a run is
ARMED, not when the config is saved.

acceptance.description: Free text — what counts as a pass.

expectedTurns.description:
How many questions this survey asks.

**The only limit that is actually enforced.** After this many
answers the conversation is disabled at the carrier, so the
"thanks for your feedback" that ends most surveys reaches a
respondent that cannot reply.

Set it here rather than per test — a survey asks the same number
of questions every time. A single run may override it.

Optional. Without it nothing is enforced, because guessing would
cut a survey short.

mission.description: Free text — what this person is doing and how they feel about it.

profileId.description: A workspace-scoped Profile, used as the persona.

scenario.description:
How the respondent behaves once the survey is under way.

A closed set, deliberately. Each value maps to wording nopaque
maintains, so the behaviour can be improved without you rewriting saved
configs, and a scenario cannot be saved that has no behaviour behind
it. Clients design for the happy path; the other four are where survey
testing earns its keep.

Answers are never scripted. A survey explains its own scale as it goes
("press 1 to 5, where 1 is least happy") and a real respondent does not
know that until they are contacted — so the config says who the person
is, and the respondent maps that onto whatever the survey presents.

sector.description: What the survey is about — customer satisfaction, meter read. You name it, not us.

voiceId.description: Voice surveys only; ignored on an SMS conversation.

title: Get Survey Test Config
